# agentcfg

Go CLI for local MCP process sharing and declarative harness/skill configuration.

- Canonical sources are strictly user-level: `~/.agentcfg/mcp.json`,
  `~/.agentcfg/agentcfg.json`, `~/.agentcfg/skills/`, and `~/.agentcfg/plugins/`.
- Never use a project's `.agentcfg/` or `.agents/` as canonical sources or
  synchronize into project-local harness configuration.
- Agent Plugins manifests and MCP files must retain the portable standard format.
- Never modify live user harness configs in tests; use temporary directories.
- Keep stdout clean for MCP stdio; diagnostics go to stderr.
- Preserve unrelated config keys and user-modified managed entries.
- No listening TCP/HTTP server. Use Unix sockets and Windows named pipes.
- Run `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` before considering a change verified.
- Bidirectional import/sync is deferred; do not silently overwrite manual edits.

**One MCP process. Multiple AI coding agents.** Share local MCP servers, route skills and manage user-level harness configuration from one Go CLI.
## What it does - **One upstream, many clients** — a local broker shares MCP processes among Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Gemini CLI. Start on demand, over private Unix sockets or Windows named pipes. - **One configuration** — configure MCPs, skills and harness availability with [Huh](https://github.com/charmbracelet/huh), then preview and explicitly confirm native sync. - **Safety first** — user-scope only; no silent replacement of native settings, with backups, ownership checks and conflict detection. - **Portable workflows** — shell completion for Bash, Zsh, Fish and PowerShell, plus Agent Plugins support. ## Install Download a precompiled release and verify its published SHA-256 checksum: **Linux / macOS** ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shaar-games/agentcfg/main/install.sh | bash ``` **Windows (PowerShell)** ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shaar-games/agentcfg/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` The binary is installed in `~/.local/bin`. Installation does **not** modify any harness or MCP configuration. [Releases](https://github.com/Shaar-games/agentcfg/releases/latest) · [Installation details](docs/releases.md) ## Get started ```sh agentcfg init # Discover existing user-level harnesses, skills and MCPs agentcfg config # Configure with arrow keys and Enter agentcfg list # Browse configured items agentcfg sync # Preview changes to native harness configuration ``` `init` asks once before importing sources and migrating the selected harnesses. After success, `~/.agentcfg` is the single source of truth: MCPs connect through the broker and skills are copied from the canonical inventory. `init --plain` is read-only; `init --yes` approves the complete migration. Opening `agentcfg config` before setup offers to run `init`. Use `agentcfg restore --plain` to preview recovery to the pre-init state, then `agentcfg restore` to confirm. Native files are checked before restoration; canonical sources and backups are archived. [Recovery details](docs/cli.md#agentcfg-restore-return-to-the-pre-init-state). Use `agentcfg mcp`, `agentcfg skill` or `agentcfg harness` to jump directly to a section; plural aliases work too. `--plain` gives noninteractive output where supported. ## Browse the configuration ## How sharing works ```text Claude Code ─┐ Codex ├─ agentcfg connect ─ private IPC ─ broker ─ MCP server × 1 Cursor ┘ ``` Choose `isolated` instead of `shared` for MCP servers requiring separate sessions. Synchronization targets user-level harness files only and never overwrites unowned entries without explicit, verified adoption. **Documentation:** [CLI](docs/cli.md) · [Configuration](docs/configuration.md) · [Synchronization](docs/synchronization.md) · [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [Completions](docs/completion.md)

# Configuration examples

These files are samples, not active configuration. The canonical JSON samples have a `.example` suffix; the plugin and standalone skill live outside the user-level `~/.agentcfg/`. Merely reading or validating them starts no subprocess and contacts no remote service.

For an existing user-level harness setup, begin with `agentcfg init --plain`
to **preview discovery of installed harness MCPs and skills**. On an interactive
terminal, `agentcfg init` uses Huh Select for actions/navigation (Enter
validates) and checkboxes only for selecting multiple availabilities. It asks
for confirmation before creating canonical sources, then **offers to apply
native synchronization after a separate preview and confirmation**. No
`--apply` flag is needed for `init`. `--plain` stays read-only, and
**`agentcfg init --yes` creates only canonical sources; it never synchronizes
native harness settings**. Scripts must separately preview with
`agentcfg sync --plain`, then explicitly run `agentcfg sync --apply --yes`
to apply native changes. Neither initialization nor the sample files silently
overwrite existing entries; verified adoption
requires backup and CAS checks, and native TOML MCP adoption is refused.
Samples remain inert and are not automatically imported during discovery.

## Chrome DevTools and Context7

Review `canonical/mcp.json.example` and `canonical/agentcfg.json.example`. To use them, merge their contents into `~/.agentcfg/mcp.json` and `~/.agentcfg/agentcfg.json` (without the `.example` suffix), after backing up existing files. agentcfg then synchronizes those sources into the selected harnesses' native configuration files. Do not replace existing canonical files wholesale.

After the merge, `agentcfg mcps --plain` shows effective MCP distribution;
`agentcfg skills --plain` shows skill availability, and `agentcfg sync --plain`
previews native changes. Review that output before `agentcfg sync --apply`.

The Chrome entry uses the real `node` executable with a JavaScript entry point, so it does not require an npm shell shim. Its explicit `"cwd": "./.agentcfg"` resolves from the user home and makes relative arguments point into `~/.agentcfg/node_modules/`. Without an explicit `cwd`, canonical servers run from the home directory. To run this example, install a compatible package under `~/.agentcfg/node_modules/` yourself or replace the script argument with the absolute JavaScript entry point of your installation. Verify the entry point against [the upstream package manifest](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/blob/main/package.json) for the version you pin. This example installs nothing.

The upstream alternative is `npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest`, with `command: "npx"` and separate arguments. On Windows, npm may expose a `.cmd` shim; agentcfg supports ordinary wrappers but rejects unsafe batch arguments as described in [transport limitations](../docs/transports.md). The supplied direct-Node form does not depend on a batch wrapper and passes the script and arguments directly to Node.

Context7 uses its documented remote endpoint. No credentials are included. Service availability, authentication and rate limits are checked when a client actually connects, not during configuration loading.

Sources: [Chrome DevTools MCP](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp) and [Context7](https://github.com/upstash/context7).

## Portable plugin

`plugins/docs-helper` is an Agent Plugins 1.0.0 package. Copy that folder to **`~/.agentcfg/plugins/docs-helper`** to discover its `docs-helper.context7` server and `docs-helper.documentation-check` skill.

The plugin contains only portable fields. The separate `canonical/agentcfg.json.example` demonstrates harness filters and sharing overrides for those qualified names. If you copy settings without the plugin, unmatched override warnings are expected; remove those overrides when you do not want the plugin.

## Standalone skill

Copy `skills/quick-review` to **`~/.agentcfg/skills/quick-review`** to discover the standalone `quick-review` skill. Its frontmatter name matches the final folder name.

For supported fields, failure boundaries and path rules, see [configuration documentation](../docs/configuration.md).

# Recorded CLI demos

The two `.tape` files record the **real agentcfg executable** with [VHS](https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs). GitHub Actions rebuilds their GIFs when the CLI or demo scripts change and commits only the generated images.

The tapes pause for at least 2.8 seconds on menus and longer on detail screens.
Repeated arrow presses are separated by 350 ms so the highlighted route is
visible. `PlaybackSpeed 0.85` also slows playback. Keep `Wait+Screen` checks
before each reading pause so slower machines do not skip a screen.

The UI follows the native Select, MultiSelect and theme patterns in the
[official Huh examples](https://github.com/charmbracelet/huh/tree/v1.0.0/examples).

The fixtures are **synthetic, inert samples**, referencing the names and public shapes of community projects:

- [Context7 MCP](https://github.com/upstash/context7) — HTTP endpoint name and URL
- [Playwright MCP](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp) — stdio command name and arguments
- [Vercel React Best Practices and Web Design Guidelines skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills) — names and minimal, original placeholder frontmatter

They are **not installed from these projects**. VHS uses an isolated `.demo/home` and exercises `agentcfg config`, `agentcfg list` and `agentcfg mcps --plain` without starting MCP processes, executing skill instructions, reaching external MCP services, or reading any real user configuration.

To reproduce on Linux with Go and Docker:

```bash
bash docs/demo/prepare.sh
go build -trimpath -o .demo/bin/agentcfg ./cmd/agentcfg
docker run --rm --network none -v "$PWD:/vhs" ghcr.io/charmbracelet/vhs docs/demo/agentcfg-config.tape
docker run --rm --network none -v "$PWD:/vhs" ghcr.io/charmbracelet/vhs docs/demo/agentcfg-list.tape
```

The workflow uploads both GIFs as a CI artifact and refreshes `docs/demo/*.gif` on `main`. Publishing a generated image does not modify the demo script or application sources.

# Architecture et garanties

## Frontends natifs, backend partagé

La synchronisation remplace seulement le lancement de chaque MCP par un relais
stdio `agentcfg connect`. Le nom de serveur reste visible dans le harness. Un
relai est nécessaire par connexion stdio, mais le processus lourd du serveur et
ses descendants sont mutualisés.

Le broker utilise un endpoint dérivé du chemin canonique de la racine source et
de l’utilisateur. Windows : named pipe protégé par une ACL pour le SID courant.
Unix : socket dans un répertoire 0700, socket 0600. Aucun port réseau d’écoute.

Un verrou de démarrage permet à plusieurs relais concurrents de vérifier puis
lancer le broker. Un deuxième verrou est conservé toute la vie du broker. Le
processus lancé est le même exécutable, en sous-commande `daemon`, détaché de la
console. Les journaux du broker se trouvent dans le répertoire cache agentcfg de
l’utilisateur ; les diagnostics ne sont jamais envoyés sur stdout des relais.

## Identité et cycle de vie

Le cache des backends utilise le nom du MCP et l’empreinte de sa configuration
résolue. Les connexions venant d’une autre racine ne partagent pas le backend.
Les variables héritées sont celles du broker à son lancement ; les overrides
explicites du serveur sont appliqués par le transport. Changer ces variables
héritées exige un arrêt puis un redémarrage du broker.

Les sources sont relues à chaque nouvelle connexion. Un changement de commande,
arguments, environnement ou URL peut donc produire une nouvelle génération.
L’ancienne continue de servir ses clients existants avant de s’éteindre après
inactivité. Les réglages d’inactivité du broker sont lus à son démarrage.

Un backend isolé est fermé dès la déconnexion de son client. Un backend partagé
reste vivant pendant `idleTimeout` sans clients. Le broker entier ferme ses
backends et quitte après sa propre inactivité. `stop` cible uniquement la racine
globale de l’utilisateur courant.

Les processus stdio sont placés dans un Job Object kill-on-close sous Windows,
avant la reprise de leur premier thread. Unix utilise un groupe de processus.
Les transports ferment leurs pipes et attendent la fin des enfants. Le broker
Windows tente le lancement breakaway pour ne pas mourir avec le Job Object du
premier harness ; si le parent refuse le détachement, un démarrage de secours
est tenté avec diagnostic explicite. Ce secours ne garantit pas la même
indépendance vis-à-vis de la durée de vie du parent.

## Multiplexage partagé

Les clients MCP 2025 utilisent l'ancien handshake stdio, mais le backend partagé
ne reçoit qu’une seule initialisation. Le résultat est conservé pour les
clients suivants. Le backend représente agentcfg, pas le premier harness :
les capacités client ambiguës roots/sampling/elicitation ne sont pas annoncées.

Les clients MCP 2026-07-28 passent directement des requêtes autonomes avec
`params._meta` et peuvent utiliser `server/discover`. Leurs identifiants sont
remappés par client sans `initialize` global. Un backend partagé ne mélange pas
les deux générations de protocole sur la même connexion stdio. Cela évite les
collisions de transport, **pas** les conflits d'état applicatif d'un MCP.

Pour chaque requête, le broker conserve le propriétaire et l’identifiant
original, génère un identifiant upstream unique, puis restaure l’identifiant au
retour. Les `progressToken` sont transformés de la même façon ; les annulations
ne ciblent que la requête du client émetteur. Les changements de listes de tools,
prompts ou resources sont diffusés aux clients initialisés. Cela ne fournit pas
une isolation des données métier d’un serveur partagé.

Les opérations globales de session — subscriptions, logging par client, tâches —
sont refusées dans ce mode. Les callbacks serveur non annoncés reçoivent une
erreur explicite. Le mode isolé transmet le protocole sans remappage vers un
backend dédié et laisse le client gérer ses capacités.

Une trame est limitée à 32 MiB, un backend à 1 024 requêtes en attente, et le
broker à 128 connexions simultanées. Un client dont la file de sortie est pleine
est déconnecté afin de ne pas bloquer les autres. Un timeout produit une erreur
et une tentative d’annulation ; il ne prouve pas qu’un effet distant a été
annulé. Aucun appel n’est rejoué automatiquement.

## Ce que les tests démontrent

Le test d’intégration lance deux vrais exécutables `agentcfg connect` avec des
identités de harness distinctes et un serveur MCP de test exécuté comme processus
enfant. Il vérifie un seul PID upstream, un seul démarrage enregistré, deux
clients dans le statut, des requêtes utilisant le même identifiant, puis la
survie du backend après fermeture d’un client. D’autres tests vérifient les PIDs
distincts en mode isolé et l’arrêt après inactivité.

Il ne s’agit pas d’un test de bout en bout de l’interface des applications
Cursor, Codex ou Claude Code. Leur configuration est vérifiée par les tests des
adaptateurs ; leurs validations de confiance, redémarrages ou activations
manuelles restent à effectuer dans ces applications.

# Command-line interface and initial setup

`agentcfg` without arguments (or `agentcfg help`) prints command help without
editing configuration. All canonical sources live under `~/.agentcfg/`.
The interactive configuration entry point is `agentcfg config`. If the canonical
settings and MCP files are missing, it offers to run initialization first.
Declining or cancelling that prompt writes nothing. If an older setup is only
partial and has never synchronized native files, the prompt offers to archive
its existing sources before initialization; it never merges or overwrites them.

## Direct configuration commands

The singular and plural forms are aliases. Each launches its section of the
same Huh interface:

| Commands | Operation | Read-only form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agentcfg harness`, `agentcfg harnesses` | Choose enabled user-level harnesses | `agentcfg harness --plain` |
| `agentcfg skill`, `agentcfg skills` | Choose which configured harnesses receive each skill | `agentcfg skills --plain` |
| `agentcfg mcp`, `agentcfg mcps` | Choose per-harness MCP availability and shared/isolated operation | `agentcfg mcps --plain` |
| `agentcfg config` | Open the compact configuration menu | Use the relevant category's `--plain` form |

Configuration and `agentcfg list` share the same six overview entries:
**Harnesses**, **MCP servers**, **Skills**, **Agent Plugins**, **Refresh** and
**Exit**. The four categories show aligned numeric counts only; Harnesses counts
the currently enabled harnesses. Refresh reloads the inventory without writing
configuration. Skill rows show enabled-harness counts; plugin rows show
MCP / skill counts, with warnings retained for invalid plugins.

Diagnostics and synchronization are not overview menu entries. Use
`agentcfg status`, `agentcfg validate` and `agentcfg sync` for those operations.

**All Huh navigation and action menus are Select fields.** Move with ↑/↓ and
press **Enter** to open the highlighted section, select an MCP or skill, or
confirm an action (including shared/isolated). No Space key is needed for a
single selection. **Only availability involving multiple harnesses, MCPs or
skills uses MultiSelect checkboxes**: Space checks/unchecks, Enter saves, and
Ctrl+C cancels. Current availability selections are prechecked. The interface
edits canonical settings; native harness files change only after an explicit
sync confirmation.

Menus show up to **ten option rows** before native Huh scrolling. Short lists
stay fully visible, and checkbox menus open at the first option while retaining
all prechecked values. Titles and wrapped descriptions have their own space.
**Back** (or **Exit** in the main menu) stays pinned below the scrollable options,
including while filtering. It occupies the tenth option row, leaving nine rows
for content. Short lists fill the gap with visual space. Arrow keys skip that space directly;
it adds no selectable entries or numbered accessible choices.
The empty space shrinks on smaller terminals so it does not cause scrolling.
Press Tab to focus the pinned action directly, including from a filter, then
Enter to activate it. Outside a filter, Esc also focuses that action.
The Harnesses checkbox screen also has a separate **Back** action: move below
the last checkbox or press Esc/Tab to focus it, then Enter to discard pending
changes and return. Enter on a checkbox still reviews the selection. Accessible
numbered mode accepts `b` followed by Enter to return without saving.
Long review notes also use a viewport of at most ten rows. Smaller terminals reduce that viewport while preserving native
scrolling and every selection. Only a terminal too small for even one content
row plus its help falls back to Huh's complete accessible list. Set `AGENTCFG_ACCESSIBLE=1` to request that mode explicitly.

Status columns align by terminal cell width, including wide Unicode labels.
Colors distinguish actions, information and warnings; `NO_COLOR` or
`CLICOLOR=0` disables navigation colors. Huh's footer supplies keyboard help.

`--plain` on a category command prints its effective settings without opening
Huh, editing sources or starting MCP processes. It is useful in scripts:

```sh
agentcfg harnesses --plain
agentcfg skill --plain
agentcfg mcps --plain
agentcfg list --plain
agentcfg validate --plain
agentcfg sync --plain         # Read-only preview of native changes
agentcfg status --json        # Machine-readable broker state
```

`--plain` controls presentation on supported commands. It does not implicitly
approve a write: `sync --apply` and any confirmation bypass such as `--yes`
are separate, explicit operations. `agentcfg config` is the interactive menu,
so use an individual category with `--plain` in a noninteractive workflow.

## `agentcfg init`: import and migrate

`agentcfg init` reads the supported user-level MCP definitions and skills,
asks which AI harnesses to enable, then requests one confirmation. Approval
imports the complete portable inventory into `~/.agentcfg/`, replaces the
selected harnesses' MCP entries with `agentcfg connect` broker proxies, and
copies the canonical skills into those harnesses' own directories.

Native MCP provenance does not restrict availability: every imported MCP is
available to all selected harnesses. Explicit skill `metadata.harness` filters
remain effective. Imported skills are removed from their old native locations,
including shared/legacy roots and unselected harnesses; selected destinations
are recreated as physical copies. Neither MCP processes nor skills are executed
during initialization. Unrelated native settings are preserved.

```sh
agentcfg init --plain                     # Read-only discovery and full details
agentcfg init                            # Choose harnesses and confirm once
agentcfg init --harnesses codex,cursor     # Set the destination selection
agentcfg init --harnesses codex,cursor --yes # Approve the complete migration
```

`--yes` authorizes both canonical creation and native migration. There is no
optional synchronization step after successful initialization. JSON/JSONC and
Codex TOML MCP entries are adopted only with revalidated scanner proofs.
Original files and skill directories are backed up for `agentcfg restore`.

The app-owned Codex desktop `node_repl` service keeps its native configuration
and private session pipes. It is listed under `Kept native` in `init --plain`,
rather than being treated as a failed user MCP import. Ordinary user MCPs named
`node_repl` are not excluded. Unsupported options are reported by MCP name and
option name, without printing their values.

Init preserves an explicitly configured `cwd` and does not add the home directory
when it is absent. Without an explicit `cwd`, a stdio MCP uses the connecting
harness's working directory. Sharing applies to clients with the same effective
working directory. After upgrading from an older broker protocol, run
`agentcfg stop` before reconnecting; status and stop remain compatible with the
older broker.

Unsupported active MCP definitions, unreadable/nonportable skills and ambiguous
names block initialization before canonical publication; `init --plain` shows
the source details. Init must not report success with a partial inventory.
A later migration failure attempts to restore the native baseline and archives
the imported canonical sources, so a failed attempt can be reviewed and retried.

After success, only `~/.agentcfg/` supplies upstream definitions and skill
content. Use `agentcfg config` to edit availability, then `agentcfg sync --plain`
and `agentcfg sync --apply` for subsequent changes. Skills are copied by default;
`sync --skill-mode auto` or `symlink` remains an explicit alternative. Native
manual edits remain conflicts, rather than being silently overwritten.

For an earlier canonical-only initialization, run `agentcfg restore` before
initializing again. Restoration preserves the old canonical data in an archive.

## Shell completion

`agentcfg completion <shell>` prints a completion script for Bash, Zsh, Fish,
PowerShell 5.1, or PowerShell 7. The accepted shell IDs are `bash`, `zsh`,
`fish`, `powershell` and `pwsh`; the last two generate the same script.
See [completion.md](completion.md) for commands to load it now or install it
persistently.

## Other useful commands

`agentcfg auth login <server>` explicitly starts an OAuth authorization
flow. `agentcfg status` inspects the broker without starting it;
`agentcfg stop` stops a running broker. `agentcfg update` updates the
executable, while `agentcfg version` prints the current version.

See the [canonical configuration](configuration.md) and
[synchronization safety](synchronization.md) references for data formats,
ownership tracking and conflict handling.

## `agentcfg restore`: return to the pre-init state

```sh
agentcfg restore --plain  # Read-only recovery preview
agentcfg restore          # Review and confirm in an interactive terminal
agentcfg restore --yes    # Explicitly approve recovery without prompts
```

New initialization writes a recovery marker alongside the canonical files.
The first native synchronization captures the files and skill trees it is
about to replace, before changing any native destination. Restoration reuses
sync's preimage checks, backups and rollback. It restores existing native MCP
configuration byte-for-byte, restores original skill directories, and removes
native destinations created by that initial synchronization.

The entire `~/.agentcfg/` directory, including later canonical edits, original
backups and recovery data, moves to `~/.agentcfg-restored-<timestamp>/`.
No canonical content is deleted. After recovery, `agentcfg init` can run again.
Native files must still match their recorded initialization output (or already
be back at their original state). A manual native edit or a later sync that
changed that output blocks recovery before any native write; it is never
silently overwritten.

A partial or canonical-only setup made by an older version can also be
archived if there is no native sync manifest or backup history. Older setups
that have already synchronized native files but have no recovery marker are
refused: the command cannot prove their pre-init state. Their existing backups
remain in `~/.agentcfg/backups/` for deliberate manual recovery.

# Shell completion

`agentcfg completion <shell>` writes a **sourceable completion script to
standard output**. Supported identifiers are `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`,
`powershell` and `pwsh`. Both PowerShell identifiers generate the same
completion registration code, compatible with Windows PowerShell 5.1 and
PowerShell 7.

Generation is local and does not inspect, create or alter configuration.
The completion covers the known commands and options; it does not
connect to MCP servers to discover dynamic names.

Make sure the installed `agentcfg` executable is on your `PATH` before
loading its completion. The commands below are **instructions to run in
your own shell**, not steps performed by the installer.

## Bash

Load completion in the current interactive Bash session:

```bash
source <(agentcfg completion bash)
```

For future interactive sessions, add that line **once** to `~/.bashrc`.
Alternatively, on systems with `bash-completion` installed and enabled,
install the generated script in the per-user completion directory:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions
agentcfg completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/agentcfg
```

Open a new Bash session after installing the script.

## Zsh

Initialize the Zsh completion system before loading the generated script:

```zsh
autoload -Uz compinit
compinit
source <(agentcfg completion zsh)
```

To enable completion every time, add `source <(agentcfg completion zsh)`
**after the existing `compinit` line** in `~/.zshrc`. If your Zsh
startup file does not initialize completion, add the three lines shown
above. Keep a single copy of the registration so the function is not
loaded repeatedly.

## Fish

Load completion in the current Fish session:

```fish
agentcfg completion fish | source
```

For persistent completion, generate a user completion file (Fish loads
files in this directory automatically):

```fish
mkdir -p ~/.config/fish/completions
agentcfg completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/agentcfg.fish
```

Open a new Fish session after installing the file.

## Windows PowerShell 5.1

Load completion in the current Windows PowerShell session:

```powershell
agentcfg completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

For future sessions, add the following line **once** to your Windows
PowerShell `$PROFILE` file:

```powershell
agentcfg completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

If `$PROFILE` does not exist, create its containing directory and an empty
profile file first:

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path -Parent $PROFILE) | Out-Null
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $PROFILE)) { New-Item -ItemType File -Path $PROFILE | Out-Null }
```

Open `$PROFILE` in your editor, add the registration line, and restart
PowerShell. An execution policy that forbids loading a profile may need
to be addressed through your normal PowerShell policy settings.

## PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`)

Load the same completion in a running PowerShell 7 session:

```powershell
agentcfg completion pwsh | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

For persistent setup, add that line once to PowerShell 7's own
`$PROFILE`. PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 may use different
profile paths; configure them separately if you use both.

## Checking the result

Start typing `agentcfg ` and press Tab. The completion offers commands
such as `config`, `init`, `harness`/`harnesses`,
`skill`/`skills` and `mcp`/`mcps`, as well as supported flags
after a subcommand.

If Tab does not suggest completions, check that `agentcfg` resolves to the
installed executable, the generated script has been loaded in the active
shell and (for Zsh) `compinit` ran first.

# Configuration and portable plugins

`config.Load(root)` reads canonical sources under `<root>/.agentcfg/`. The public CLI uses the user's home directory as `root` and synchronizes definitions through native harness configuration adapters. Loading returns resolved servers, discovered skills, settings and warnings without executing processes, looking up executables, contacting networks, creating directories or writing harness configuration.

## Sources

| Location relative to root | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.agentcfg/mcp.json` | Explicit canonical MCP servers and optional agentcfg fields |
| `.agentcfg/agentcfg.json` | Selected harnesses, runtime durations and named overrides |
| `.agentcfg/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` | Standalone skills |
| `.agentcfg/plugins/<folder>/plugin.json` | Required portable plugin manifest |
| `.agentcfg/plugins/<folder>/mcp.json` | Optional portable MCP component |
| `.agentcfg/plugins/<folder>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` | Optional portable skills |

Only immediate plugin directories and immediate skill directories are discovered. The manifest name, rather than the installation folder name, supplies a plugin's namespace. Missing optional sources are valid. The source root itself must exist and be a directory.

`agentcfg` without arguments displays help. `agentcfg config` opens the Huh
configuration interface. **Navigation and action choices use Huh Select**
(↑/↓ to navigate, **Enter to validate**). **Only multi-value availability**
for harnesses, MCPs and skills uses MultiSelect checkboxes (Space to toggle,
Enter to save, Ctrl+C to cancel). The direct section commands are
`agentcfg harness` / `harnesses`, `agentcfg skill` / `skills` and
`agentcfg mcp` / `mcps`; both spellings in each pair have the same meaning.
Each accepts `--plain` to display effective configuration without writing.
See [CLI usage](cli.md) for commands and [completion](completion.md) for Bash,
Zsh, Fish and PowerShell setup.

### Initial discovery

`agentcfg init` discovers supported, user-level native MCP entries and skill
directories from installed harnesses. On an interactive terminal, it uses
Huh Select for navigation/actions and checkboxes only for multi-availability
choices, previews the proposal, and requests confirmation **before creating
canonical sources**. It does not execute discovered MCPs or skills.
`agentcfg init --plain` produces only a read-only discovery preview.

Credentials in environment variables, arguments, URLs and headers are copied
unchanged into `~/.agentcfg/mcp.json`. Yellow warnings are informational and do
not block initialization or add a confirmation. Variable expressions are also
copied literally; agentcfg does not evaluate harness-specific substitutions.
Invalid definitions and unsupported options still require correction rather
than silently losing configuration.
Client-side timing settings (`timeout` in OpenCode/Gemini and
`startup_timeout_sec`, `startup_timeout_ms`, `tool_timeout_sec` in Codex) are
omitted with a nonblocking warning. Agentcfg's runtime deadlines apply after
import; the original native values remain in the initialization restore point.

A single confirmation approves the complete initialization: canonical import,
broker proxies in selected harnesses, and physical skill copies. `init --yes`
explicitly approves the same migration without prompts; `init --plain` remains
read-only. There is no successful canonical-only init mode.

Identical definitions with the same MCP name are imported once, across harnesses
and across multiple files of the same harness. Different definitions sharing a
name are preserved separately, with a harness suffix and a definition hash when
needed; a warning reports the names. Initialization synchronizes all existing
OpenCode user JSON/JSONC locations, including legacy locations, and subsequent
syncs track each file. Restore recovers each original file byte for byte.

Imported MCPs are available to the globally selected harnesses by default;
their former location is provenance, not an availability filter. Native disable
flags become canonical availability filters: a fully disabled MCP stays disabled,
and a copy disabled only in one harness is not enabled there. If a harness has
both active and inactive copies of the same definition, its active copy wins.
Disable-only overrides, including disabled-server lists without an MCP section,
are retired when a complete definition was also imported.
Only imported names are removed from native disabled-server lists; unrelated
policies remain unchanged.

All portable native skills are centralized, including skills from unselected harnesses, and copied
according to their explicit `metadata.harness` filters. Their original locations
are backed up and retired. JSON/JSONC and Codex TOML adoption preserve unrelated
native settings. Incomplete imports and concurrent edits block initialization;
a failed migration attempts to restore the native baseline and archives its
canonical imports for review. `agentcfg restore` reverses a completed init.
Subsequent managed synchronizations update the expected generated state while
keeping the original restore baseline. This includes adding or removing MCPs,
changing skills and enabling another harness. Failed writes roll back their
restore checkpoint and newly created empty native directories. Unrelated manual
native edits remain protected: synchronization preserves them, and restore
refuses to overwrite a native file that diverged from its recorded state.


The Windows Codex desktop `node_repl` runtime is preserved in its native config
when its bundled executable and private session-pipe configuration identify it.
It remains managed by Codex, does not block user MCP imports, and is not copied
to other harnesses. A custom MCP merely named `node_repl` is still imported.
`init --plain` lists preserved runtimes separately from import failures.

The configuration loader itself remains read-only. Initialization is an
explicit CLI operation that reads supported installed harness locations and
asks before writing; it does not change the semantics of `config.Load`.

## Canonical MCP servers

~~~json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "local-tools": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["./tools/server.mjs"],
      "env": {"LOG_LEVEL": "info"},
      "harnesses": ["claude-code", "codex"],
      "sharing": "shared"
    },
    "documentation": {
      "type": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://example.com/mcp",
      "sharing": "isolated"
    }
  }
}
~~~

The root object accepts `mcpServers` and an optional `$schema`. If present, the schema identifier must be the supported MCP identifier shown below. Canonical server objects can add `harnesses` and `sharing`; those additions are agentcfg configuration, not part of the portable plugin schema.

| Transport | Required fields | Optional fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stdio` | `command` | `args`, `env`, `cwd` |
| `streamable-http` | `url` | `headers` |

An omitted canonical `type` is inferred from `command` or, if no command is supplied, `url`. A plugin must declare its type explicitly. Fields belonging to another transport and other unknown fields invalidate that entry. Legacy `sse` entries produce a warning and are skipped; this does not prohibit SSE responses belonging to Streamable HTTP.

`command` is an executable token and `args` is an array of separate strings. The loader does not construct a shell command. Bare executables are left for the launcher to resolve. Canonical path commands may be absolute or relative to the source root and must resolve to regular files. An omitted canonical `cwd` remains unset: the MCP inherits the connecting client's working directory. An explicit relative value resolves from the source root and must already be a directory. Shared stdio processes are grouped by their effective working directory; clients in different projects do not reuse the same process unless they configure a common explicit `cwd`. Machine-specific absolute paths are allowed in canonical configuration.

Environment names must be nonempty, contain neither NUL nor `=`, and be unique ignoring case. Argument and environment values cannot contain NUL bytes. These checks do not interpret arguments as filesystem paths.

## Harness selection and overrides

The default settings are:

~~~json
{
  "harnesses": ["claude-code", "codex", "cursor", "opencode", "gemini"],
  "runtime": {
    "idleTimeout": "5m",
    "requestTimeout": "5m"
  },
  "serverOverrides": {}
}
~~~

`antigravity` is also accepted and targets `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` and `~/.gemini/config/skills/`, the Google Antigravity personal layout. VS Code has no supported user-scope adapter: `agentcfg init --harnesses vscode` refuses this selection. Duplicate harness names are removed while retaining their order. Unknown names are errors.

Runtime durations use Go duration syntax, such as `30s` or `5m`, and must be positive. An omitted field retains its default.

The global `harnesses` list selects sync destinations. An explicit empty global list selects none. A server or skill filter narrows those destinations. An omitted filter allows all selected harnesses. For skills, `metadata.harness: none` represents an explicitly empty selection. Direct CLI connections with no harness name are allowed by `config.Allows`; these filters are routing preferences, not authorization controls.

Use fully qualified plugin IDs in overrides:

~~~json
{
  "harnesses": ["claude-code", "codex", "antigravity"],
  "serverOverrides": {
    "docs-helper.context7": {
      "harnesses": ["codex", "claude-code"],
      "sharing": "isolated"
    }
  }
}
~~~

Server overrides replace only fields explicitly present. For example, `"harnesses": []` clears a narrower filter. `sharing` accepts exactly `shared` or `isolated`; an empty string is invalid. Skills use `metadata.harness` in their own SKILL.md, not settings overrides.

`shared` is the server default and requests a shared upstream instance. `isolated` requests a separate upstream connection for each client. Choose the latter when an MCP relies on private session state or client callbacks; see the runtime documentation for the supported shared-session operations.

Skills are distributed into each selected harness's own directory; Codex uses `~/.codex/skills/` (its [supported legacy user location](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/skills/src/host_roots.rs)), rather than the shared `~/.agents/skills/`. During initialization, imported skills from every native location are backed up and removed after their canonical copies have been verified; enabled destinations are replaced with physical copies. Existing agentcfg-managed shared skills migrate on the next sync. Unimported skills and manually modified managed entries are protected. `agentcfg restore` restores the original shared imports when an initialization restore point exists.

Initialization follows existing user-declared symlinks and Windows junctions,
including shared skills roots, individual skills, nested assets, MCP files and
linked harness directories. Targets may be elsewhere on disk; only the declared
user harness locations are discovered, never project configurations. Sources are
snapshotted before any shared alias is detached. Imported content becomes
physical canonical copies, then physical copies or broker entries in the selected
harnesses. Independent external targets remain unchanged.

`agentcfg restore` restores the original entries, including relative links and
junction types, by moving the saved entries back. Unrelated files in a linked
harness directory are preserved. A changed source, changed backup or manual edit
blocks replacement. Broken links, cycles, special files and trees exceeding the
snapshot limits produce an error before their native entries are replaced.
Layout staging stays in the private `~/.agentcfg/restore/layout/` directory,
outside native skill discovery. Windows rename sharing/access conflicts are
retried for up to five seconds, with identity, content and ownership checks
repeated before retrying. Cancellation returns through rollback; persistent locks
or permission errors leave the originals and recovery data intact. No permissions
are elevated or protections disabled. Older restore journals with sibling staging
paths remain readable.

Native layout snapshots are bounded to 100,000 entries, 512 MiB total and 64 MiB
per file; the smaller skill discovery limits still apply to imported skills.

The canonical sources remain under `~/.agentcfg/skills/`. Harness-native discovery can still read additional locations independently of agentcfg; distribution filters are not an isolation or authorization boundary.

## Portable manifests

A minimal `plugin.json` is:

~~~json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json",
  "name": "docs-helper"
}
~~~

The required name uses 1–64 ASCII lowercase letters, numbers, dots or hyphens, begins and ends with an alphanumeric character, and contains neither `--` nor `..`. Optional metadata fields are `version`, `description`, `author`, `homepage`, `repository`, `license`, `keywords` and `extensions`.

Metadata is checked by its specified JSON type. Version, URL, email and license strings are not rejected for lacking a particular external format. An author object permits only string fields `name`, `email` and `url`; keywords must be strings.

The author schema is closed, but the normative client rules specify two recovery cases: **report and ignore unknown top-level manifest fields**, and **report and ignore non-object extensions**. Other manifest violations reject that plugin. agentcfg does not implement extension namespaces, so their values are ignored without assigning semantics. Unknown manifest fields never override the fixed component locations. These recovery rules follow [loading and discovery](https://agent-plugins.org/client-implementers/loading-and-discovery) and [specification §§5.2 and 8.1](https://agent-plugins.org/specification).

## Portable MCP components

~~~json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json",
  "mcpServers": {
    "context7": {
      "type": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://mcp.context7.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
~~~

Both `$schema` and `mcpServers` are required, and no other top-level fields are permitted. Each server uses the closed portable transport variant. Thus `harnesses`, `sharing`, `disabled` and inline client options invalidate a portable server entry; put agentcfg preferences in the external overrides file.

For this example the resolved identifier is `docs-helper.context7`. A plugin's skill `documentation-check` becomes `docs-helper.documentation-check` internally. Its original skill name and source frontmatter remain unchanged.

agentcfg recognizes Agent Plugins 1.0.0 locally. It never fetches a declared schema while loading. Unsupported or mismatched component schema identifiers disable the relevant plugin/component.

## Plugin paths and variables

Canonical directories, plugin catalogs, packages and their read-only components may use explicit symlinks or Windows junctions, including external targets. Manifest, MCP, command, working-directory and skill paths must remain lexically inside their declared package; existing links are resolved for reading. Synchronization copies skill contents into physical destination trees. Writable plugin data retains its dedicated containment checks.

On Windows, the shared path resolver obtains the final path through a metadata handle and [GetFinalPathNameByHandle](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getfinalpathnamebyhandlew). This also resolves directory junctions that the standard Go path helper can leave at their apparent location.

For plugin stdio servers:

| Field | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| `command` | Bare executable name, or a package path beginning `./` |
| omitted `cwd` | Resolved plugin root |
| `cwd: "./work"` | Existing directory inside the plugin |
| `cwd: "${PLUGIN_ROOT}/work"` | Existing directory inside the plugin |
| `cwd: "${PLUGIN_DATA}"` or a child | Dedicated data directory; may be absent during load |
| `args` and environment values | Opaque strings with the two supported substitutions |

Portable paths use forward slashes; explicit backslashes and drive/stream colons in package-relative fields are rejected. Traversal outside the declared package invalidates that entry; an explicit existing link may refer to an external read target. A package command must resolve to a regular file.

`${PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${PLUGIN_DATA}` are replaced textually, in one non-recursive pass, in arguments, environment values and working directories. Unknown placeholders stay literal. Replacement never applies to commands, environment keys, URLs or headers, and does not expand arbitrary host environment variables.

The launcher receives reserved `PLUGIN_ROOT` and `PLUGIN_DATA` environment variables. Plugin-defined replacements, including case variants, are rejected. Data is assigned to:

~~~text
<user-home>/.agentcfg/data/plugins/<manifest-name>
~~~

That location remains stable across updates using the same manifest name. Existing data paths must be directories, remain within the source root, and must not alias another plugin's data directory. The loader computes missing paths without creating them. The process launcher is responsible for creating the data directory and a selected data-rooted working directory immediately before launch.

Lexical path checks reject package traversal during this load. They do not sandbox a subprocess or freeze a filesystem against later changes. Arguments and environment values remain opaque even when they look like paths.

## Remote URLs and headers

URLs must be absolute HTTP(S), have a valid host/port, and contain no fragment. Literal URL credentials and HTTP endpoints are accepted; native import warns without blocking. IPv6 literals use brackets. Empty/invalid ports, malformed authorities and unsupported URL schemes invalidate only their entry. OAuth issuer, metadata and callback URLs retain their separate validation requirements.

Headers are literal string maps with valid HTTP names and values. Duplicate names ignoring case and control-character injection are rejected. Portable headers are visible package data and should not contain credentials. Agent Plugins 1.0.0 defines no portable OAuth or credential-reference fields; the loader does not perform authentication. See the [MCP component specification](https://agent-plugins.org/plugin-authors/mcp-servers).

## Skills

Both standalone and plugin skills require a regular `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter:

~~~markdown
---
name: documentation-check
description: Check official documentation when a task depends on a library API.
metadata:
  harness: codex,claude-code,cursor
---
Read the relevant documentation and cite the version used.
~~~

The name must match its discovered directory basename, use 1–64 lowercase Unicode letters, digits or hyphens, and have no leading, trailing or doubled hyphen. The description must be a nonempty string of at most 1,024 characters. The optional `license` and `allowed-tools` fields are strings; `compatibility` is a string of 1–500 characters; `metadata` is a string-to-string map. Additional frontmatter fields are parsed safely but receive no agentcfg semantics.

BOM and CRLF input are supported. Duplicate YAML keys, aliases, anchors, custom tags, malformed types and missing delimiters reject only the affected skill. No skill instructions or scripts are executed by loading.

The full skill tree is checked for broken links, cycles, size limits and special files because sync may copy that tree. Explicit links, including nested assets and a linked `SKILL.md`, are read and expanded into physical copies during sync. Aliases retain the discovered basename for installation, even when the filesystem target has a different name.

These are explicit implementation limits: configuration/skill files are limited to 1 MiB, frontmatter to 64 KiB, YAML to 32 levels and 4,096 nodes, and one skill tree to 10,000 visited entries.

Standalone directories containing the reserved `.agentcfg-origin.json` marker are generated copies and are skipped. Standalone links into the plugin source tree or a loaded plugin root are also skipped to avoid rediscovering materialized plugin skills. A rejected plugin cannot suppress unrelated standalone skills.

## Errors and precedence

| Failure | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid source root, settings, or top-level canonical MCP document | `Load` returns an error |
| Invalid canonical server | Warning; other entries continue |
| Invalid/missing plugin manifest | Warning; that plugin is skipped |
| Invalid plugin MCP document or fixed component path | Warning; that component is skipped |
| Invalid plugin server or individual skill | Warning; its siblings continue |
| Missing optional plugin component | No error |
| Duplicate qualified server ID | Warning; first valid entry wins |
| Duplicate plugin manifest name | Warning; first valid plugin directory wins |

Explicit canonical servers load first and take precedence over colliding plugin IDs. Plugin directory names and server keys are processed lexically. Skills are returned sorted by qualified name. Duplicate keys are rejected at their owning JSON object boundary; semantic errors inside one server do not invalidate its siblings.

The loader does not install packages, execute client extensions, synchronize native configurations in either direction, or infer secrets. Bidirectional configuration import is not implemented.

# Releases and installers

## Supported binaries

GitHub Actions builds precompiled, CGO-free binaries:

| OS | CPU | Release asset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux | AMD64 | `agentcfg_linux_amd64.tar.gz` |
| Linux | ARM64 | `agentcfg_linux_arm64.tar.gz` |
| macOS | AMD64 | `agentcfg_darwin_amd64.tar.gz` |
| macOS | ARM64 | `agentcfg_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` |
| Windows | AMD64 | `agentcfg_windows_amd64.zip` |
| Windows | ARM64 | `agentcfg_windows_arm64.zip` |

Each release includes `SHA256SUMS` with the SHA-256 of every archive.

## Installation

The install scripts require **Bash** on Unix or **PowerShell** on Windows.
They never invoke Go, Git, npm, Node, Python, mise or a local build.
They select the OS and architecture, download one archive and its checksum
manifest from the latest GitHub Release, verify the archive, extract the
executable, and install it into `~/.local/bin/`. Reinstalling **replaces**
the existing executable after checking the archive and staged binary. A
temporary backup is kept until the new binary passes its version smoke test.
On Windows, an old running executable may leave a backup that can be removed
after the process exits. The installer targets only `agentcfg` (`agentcfg.exe`
on Windows), without modifying MCP or harness configuration.

Set `AGENTCFG_VERSION` to an existing published release tag to select a
specific version.
Set `AGENTCFG_BIN_DIR` for a custom user-owned destination.
`AGENTCFG_RELEASE_BASE_URL` is used by local installer test fixtures and
normally should remain unset.

## Self-update

```sh
agentcfg update
```

The command queries the latest **stable GitHub Release targeting `main`**,
downloads the platform archive plus `SHA256SUMS`, checks the SHA-256 digest,
extracts only the expected executable, verifies that it reports the release
version, and replaces the executable currently running agentcfg. It does not
touch native harness configurations, MCP definitions or skills. No Go toolchain
is required.

Unix uses a same-filesystem atomic rename and a backup for rollback. Windows
renames the old executable before installing the replacement, so an active
agentcfg process can keep using its already-mapped image. If Windows cannot
delete that backup while it remains in use, its path is printed for cleanup
after the updater exits. Failure before replacement leaves the existing binary
untouched; a failed installed-binary smoke test triggers restoration.

**Checksum verification is not publisher authentication.** Since the checksum
comes from the same GitHub Release as the binary, a compromised release could
replace both. Signed provenance/attestations are potential future enhancements.

## Publishing a version

1. Confirm the CI matrix is green on the intended commit.
2. Create and push an annotated semantic version tag such as `v0.2.0`.
3. `.github/workflows/release.yml` verifies the successful complete CI matrix
   for that exact commit, builds all six targets, generates
   `SHA256SUMS`, and attaches the assets to a GitHub Release.
4. The release workflow runs a post-publication installer smoke matrix on
   Linux, macOS and Windows, downloading real release artifacts and checking
   both successful installation and successful replacement of an existing agentcfg binary.
   The checksum, `agentcfg version` and no-argument CLI help are verified as part of installation.

The release workflow also accepts a manual trigger with an existing tag.
To retry a release after a workflow-only fix, dispatch the current `main`
workflow with that existing tag. Every build and installer still checks out
the immutable tag; published assets are never overwritten.
The release gate requires a completed successful trusted CI run for the exact
tagged commit, including Linux race/format checks and all Linux, Windows and
macOS tests, builds and help checks. It rejects missing, skipped or failed
checks, unrelated commits and pull-request runs. Reusing this completed matrix
avoids acquiring a second macOS runner before building the same verified code.
Publishing requires GitHub Actions `contents: write` permission only for
the publish job. Never publish artifacts built from uncommitted local changes.

Once installed and available on `PATH`, the executable can generate
[shell completion](completion.md) for Bash, Zsh, Fish, Windows PowerShell
and PowerShell 7. The installation scripts do not edit shell profiles.

Non implémentée. La détection de modifications manuelles actuelle doit rester
la base du mécanisme de conflits. Un futur import devra distinguer les entrées
personnelles des relais générés et reconstruire la configuration upstream, pas
importer `agentcfg connect` comme serveur réel.

Prévoir une fusion à trois versions : canonique actuelle, dernière projection
connue et configuration native actuelle. Les suppressions, renommages, filtres,
secrets, changements d’arguments et collisions entre harnesses devront être
présentés dans un plan explicite. Aucun « dernier écrivain gagne » silencieux.

# Synchronisation et propriété des fichiers

## Autorité

Les fichiers canoniques `~/.agentcfg/mcp.json`, `~/.agentcfg/agentcfg.json`, les plugins
et les skills sous `~/.agentcfg/` sont les seules sources d’autorité. `sync` prépare un plan en
lecture seule. `sync --apply` applique ce plan. Il n’existe ni import implicite,
ni mode force, ni fusion bidirectionnelle dans cette version.

agentcfg projette ces sources dans les **fichiers de configuration natifs** des
harnesses sélectionnés. Ouvrir `agentcfg config` pour choisir les destinations
et les skills dans les listes Huh, puis examiner `agentcfg sync` avant toute
application avec `agentcfg sync --apply`.

Lors de la première configuration, `agentcfg init` importe les MCP et skills
natifs dans `~/.agentcfg/`, remplace les MCP des harnesses sélectionnés par les
proxies du broker et copie les skills depuis les sources canoniques. Une seule
confirmation autorise ce parcours complet. `init --yes` autorise la même
migration sans formulaire ; `init --plain` reste une prévisualisation sans écriture.
Après un init réussi, `~/.agentcfg/` est la seule source de vérité. Les imports
conservent les credentials et les expressions de variables à l'identique dans
`mcp.json` ; les avertissements jaunes ne bloquent pas la migration et ne
demandent aucune confirmation supplémentaire. Les substitutions propres aux
harnesses ne sont pas interprétées par agentcfg. Les imports
incomplets ou ambigus bloquent l'initialisation ; un échec de migration tente de
restaurer l'état natif et archive les sources importées pour permettre un nouvel essai.

Le runtime Windows `node_repl` fourni par l'application Codex reste géré par
Codex : son exécutable intégré et ses paramètres de pipe privé l'identifient.
Il ne bloque pas l'import des MCP utilisateur et n'est pas distribué aux autres
harnesses. `init --plain` le signale séparément ; un MCP utilisateur portant
simplement le même nom n'est pas exclu.

Un `cwd` absent reste absent des sources canoniques. Le processus MCP hérite du
dossier du client lors de la connexion ; aucun home n'est ajouté par init. Les
clients d'un même dossier peuvent partager le processus ; des dossiers différents
restent des contextes séparés, sauf `cwd` explicite commun.

Les menus d'action et de navigation sont des **Huh Select** : les flèches
choisissent et **Entrée valide directement**. Les cases à cocher (MultiSelect)
servent uniquement à choisir plusieurs disponibilités de harnesses, skills
ou MCP. Elles se cochent/décochent avec Espace.

Les fichiers canoniques existants, les entrées natives non gérées et les skills
déjà présents ne sont **jamais écrasés silencieusement**. Un conflit de nom ou
une modification concurrente bloque l'opération concernée. Pour une
prévisualisation ordinaire ultérieure, `agentcfg sync --plain` produit une
sortie sans formulaire ; l'écriture nécessite toujours `--apply`.

L'initialisation adopte uniquement les entrées prouvées par le scanner, avec
sauvegarde et revalidation CAS : MCP JSON/JSONC ou TOML Codex, et arbres de skills
identiques à leur copie canonique. Les définitions upstream restent dans
`~/.agentcfg/mcp.json` ; les fichiers natifs utilisent `agentcfg connect`.
Les skills importés sont retirés de leurs emplacements d'origine, y compris
ceux des harnesses non sélectionnés, puis copiés dans les destinations activées.
Les autres clés de configuration native sont conservées.

Un serveur MCP est généré individuellement dans chaque harness sélectionné.
Les filtres de l’entrée canonique et les overrides des plugins sont évalués
avant la génération. Un filtre vide signifie tous les harnesses globalement
sélectionnés ; une sélection globale vide retire seulement les éléments déjà
gérés et inchangés lors de la prochaine application.

## Éditions conservatrices

Le manifeste de propriété `~/.agentcfg/sync-user.json`
conserve les chemins et empreintes des entrées générées. Il ne contient pas la
configuration upstream ni ses secrets. Supprimer ce manifeste ne réinitialise
pas magiquement les fichiers : les entrées restantes redeviennent inconnues et
leurs collisions sont refusées.

Pour JSON/JSONC, les patches ciblent chaque entrée sous `mcpServers`, `mcp` ou
`servers`. Les commentaires sont conservés, même si l’indentation est normalisée
lors d’une modification. Pour TOML, un bloc délimité par commentaires contient
les tables générées ; les octets en dehors de ce bloc sont conservés. Modifier
ce bloc à la main produit un conflit, y compris pour ses commentaires.

Le plan refuse une entrée de même nom qu’il ne possède pas, un contenu géré
modifié ou supprimé manuellement, un chemin cible traversant un lien, ou une
destination de skill ambiguë. Les fichiers existants et leurs empreintes sont
revérifiés avant l’écriture. Les suppressions ne concernent que les éléments
gérés restés inchangés.

L’application utilise un verrou par portée, des écritures par fichier temporaire
puis renommage, et des sauvegardes sous `~/.agentcfg/backups/<date>/`. Une erreur
d’écriture déclenche une tentative de restauration des changements déjà faits.
Ce n’est pas une transaction de système de fichiers globale : une coupure
machine pendant l’application peut nécessiter une restauration depuis ces
sauvegardes. Une restauration ne remplace pas un fichier modifié concurremment.

## Skills

Le dossier complet d’un skill est lié ou copié, pas seulement `SKILL.md`.
`copy` est le mode par défaut de la CLI. Le mode explicite `auto` tente un lien symbolique et copie si le système le refuse. `symlink`
refuse de continuer lorsqu’un lien n’est pas disponible. `copy` convient lorsque
le harness ou le système ne suit pas les liens. Aucune réécriture des noms du
frontmatter n’est effectuée ; les collisions entre noms natifs doivent être
résolues dans les sources.

La source `~/.agentcfg/skills/` est distincte des destinations natives, notamment
`~/.codex/skills/` pour Codex (emplacement utilisateur historique encore pris en charge). Le contenu de chaque fichier du skill source,
dont `SKILL.md`, est conservé octet pour octet en mode copie. Aucun fichier de
marquage n'est ajouté aux nouvelles copies. Les anciens marqueurs
`.agentcfg-origin.json` restent reconnus à la lecture pour compatibilité.

Les liens internes dans un arbre de skill ne sont pas synchronisés dans cette
version, même lorsqu’ils restent dans le plugin. Cela évite les copies ambiguës
ou les références qui s’échappent de la destination. Un dossier source complet
peut en revanche être résolu avant création du lien de destination.

Les skills importés depuis `~/.agents/skills/` sont retirés de ce dossier partagé
pendant init, après vérification de leur copie canonique. Les anciennes distributions gérées à cet emplacement migrent lors du
prochain sync. Les originaux sont sauvegardés ; `restore` peut les remettre à leur
place grâce au point de restauration initial. Aucun skill non importé ni aucune
modification manuelle ne sont effacés.

Les filtres ne peuvent pas empêcher un harness de scanner de lui-même d’autres
emplacements. Ils ne constituent donc pas une ACL. Les sources canoniques ne
sont jamais supprimées pour contourner le scanner natif d’un logiciel.

## Portée utilisateur

Les instructions canoniques `~/.agentcfg/AGENTS.md` sont synchronisées en portée
utilisateur vers `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` et
`~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`, sous réserve du filtre YAML `metadata.harness`.
La source est préservée ; le frontmatter propre à agentcfg est retiré des copies
générées. Les fichiers natifs non gérés ne sont jamais écrasés, et une modification
concurrente empêche l'application. Les autres harnesses reçoivent un avertissement
tant qu'aucune destination d'instructions utilisateur n'est vérifiée.

La CLI publique synchronise exclusivement les fichiers du home courant :
Claude utilise `.claude.json`, Codex
`.codex/config.toml`, Cursor `.cursor/mcp.json`, Gemini `.gemini/settings.json`

# Upstream transports

`internal/upstream.Start(ctx, server, stderr)` opens one upstream connection for
the backend lifetime. It does not initialize MCP itself: the broker sends
`initialize` and `notifications/initialized`, decides sharing policy and routes
request IDs, callbacks and progress notifications.

```go
type Transport interface {
    Read() (wire.Message, error)
    Write(wire.Message) error
    Close() error
    PID() int
}
```

Use one reader. Concurrent writes and repeated/concurrent closes are supported.
Closing cancels outstanding I/O and waits for the transport's workers. A supplied
stderr writer must return promptly from `Write`; arbitrary blocking application
writers cannot be interrupted through the `io.Writer` interface. The transport
never closes that supplied writer. `PID()` is the actual direct process PID for
stdio and zero for HTTP.

## Stdio

The executable and argument array are separate. Native executables are launched
directly, with no shell expression evaluation. The resolved working directory
and a deterministic merge of the inherited environment and server overrides are
used for execution and executable lookup. Windows environment names are matched
case-insensitively; if override spellings collide, the lexically last spelling
wins. No implicit current-directory executable search is added: name lookup uses
the configured `PATH` and Windows `PATHEXT`. Paths containing spaces are supported.

If a canonical stdio server omits `cwd`, the connection supplies its caller's
working directory over private IPC. The broker resolves that directory before
selecting an upstream process, so its own launch directory cannot leak into a
later client's context. An explicit server `cwd` takes precedence. Clients with
the same resolved configuration and directory can share; different directories
produce different backend identities. No project-local canonical files are read
or written to establish this runtime context.

When the **server configuration** supplies a nonempty `PLUGIN_DATA`, execution
creates that directory and, if needed, a selected working directory beneath it.
Configuration discovery does not create directories. Merely inheriting
`PLUGIN_DATA` from the broker environment does not create it. A missing working
directory outside the configured data directory is an error.

Windows processes start suspended and hidden. Only private duplicates of the
three child pipe handles are inherited. A kill-on-close Job Object is configured
and the suspended process is attached before its primary thread is resumed. If
job creation, restriction, assignment or resumption fails, startup fails and any
created process is terminated and waited for. The job does not grant child
breakaway permission. Closing the job terminates its descendants, including
children started by `.cmd` wrappers. The parent process handle is always waited
for and released.

On Unix, the process starts in a new process group. Close sends `SIGKILL` to that
group and waits for the direct child. This covers descendants that remain in the
group; a program deliberately creating a separate session/group can escape that
mechanism. It is process cleanup, not an operating-system sandbox.

If the direct process exits naturally, remaining group/job members are stopped,
but buffered stdout remains readable. This preserves the last JSON-RPC response.
Stdin and stdout use the shared bounded newline framing: a JSON-RPC object is at
most **32 MiB**. Malformed or oversized input fails the read. Child stderr stays
separate from protocol stdout.

### Windows batch wrappers

`.cmd` and `.bat` require the system `cmd.exe`. The transport uses an explicit
system interpreter, disables AutoRun and delayed expansion, and quotes the
resolved script and every argument. This supports ordinary `npx.cmd` style
wrappers and script paths/arguments containing spaces, ampersands, pipes,
parentheses and carets without treating those argument characters as commands.

Batch arguments containing a double quote, `%`, `!`, NUL or a line break are
rejected before launch. Arguments ending in a backslash are also rejected
because cmd and an executable called through `%*` interpret that quoting
differently. A batch script path containing those unsafe characters is rejected.
For these values, configure the underlying executable directly, such as
`node.exe` plus the JavaScript entry point and its argument array. Native
executables retain native argument quoting, including quotes, percent signs,
exclamation marks and trailing backslashes. The transport does not make the
contents of an arbitrary batch script safe; it prevents configuration arguments
from breaking its own command invocation.

## Outbound Streamable HTTP

`type: "streamable-http"` selects this transport. The URL
must be one absolute HTTP(S) MCP endpoint without URL userinfo or fragments. All
POST, GET and DELETE requests use that endpoint. Redirects are rejected, including
same-origin redirects; authentication headers are never forwarded to a redirect
target. No TCP/HTTP listener is opened by this implementation. Local test servers
exist only inside `httptest` fixtures.

Configured headers are copied for each request. MCP content, session and protocol
headers are managed by the transport; configuration cannot override the host or
connection framing. HTTP session IDs are distinct from JSON-RPC request IDs.

Each outgoing message becomes one POST. Requests accept either one JSON response
or an SSE stream that may contain notifications and server callbacks before the
matching response. Callback responses and notifications expect HTTP 202. Errors
for outgoing requests are delivered by `Read` as JSON-RPC errors with the original
request ID. Failed notifications/responses terminate the transport because there
is no request ID to which an error could be returned. Transport-generated errors
omit URLs, configured headers, response bodies and underlying network error text.
Raw valid MCP messages, including server-supplied error responses, retain their
content for the broker.

Initialization response headers are retained before parsing its SSE events, so
callbacks during initialization can use the session. The negotiated protocol
version and successful session state are installed before exposing the initialize
result. Later POSTs and the optional GET stream wait for the initialized
notification's HTTP acceptance. Subsequent requests include `Mcp-Session-Id`, when
assigned, and `MCP-Protocol-Version`. A session-bearing HTTP 404 ends the transport;
reconnection must start a fresh initialization. Tool requests are never replayed.

After initialization, one optional GET SSE stream receives unsolicited requests
and notifications. HTTP 405/501 or an unsupported GET response disables that
optional channel while POST remains available. A clean GET EOF reconnects after
one second. GET streams rotate after five minutes and are cancelled at close.
Malformed GET streams and other GET failures disable the optional channel, except
session expiration or a decoded message that cannot be delivered before its
deadline: those failures end the session instead of silently dropping that data.

The SSE reader handles LF, CRLF and bare CR, a leading UTF-8 BOM, comments,
multiline `data` fields, empty priming events and events split across reads. It
requires a complete event delimiter; an incomplete event at EOF is discarded.
Both a line and the total encoded event are bounded by 32 MiB, including framing
overhead. JSON responses and outgoing messages are also bounded by 32 MiB.
Request-ID matching preserves number/string distinctions, arbitrary integer
precision and equivalent string escapes; the original encoding is used when
delivering the correlated response to the broker.

### Bounds, cancellation and shutdown

- At most eight request POSTs and four separate control/reply POSTs are active.
  No goroutine is started before a slot is reserved. A saturated lane makes
  `Write` return `ErrBusy` immediately. The broker must handle that write error.
- Separate control capacity lets callback replies and cancellation proceed even
  when all request slots hold streams awaiting a reply.
- The receive queue contains at most eight messages. Backpressure observes the
  operation context. If a failed/cancelled request's completion cannot be queued,
  the transport terminates so the operation does not leave a blocked worker.
- A POST has a two-minute overall deadline, including response headers and body.
  The dial and TLS handshake deadlines are ten seconds. Backend context
  cancellation interrupts all active operations.
- `notifications/cancelled` is forwarded to the server and cancels the matching
  local POST, except initialization. Local cancellation is not proof that the
  remote operation stopped; it may already have executed.
- Close cancels active operations, waits for workers, attempts session DELETE
  with a fresh context bounded to two seconds, and closes idle connections.
  DELETE errors and HTTP 405 are best effort and do not prevent local cleanup.

### Modern MCP 2026-07-28 (stateless)

In addition to the 2025 initialization/session protocol, the transport accepts
requests carrying the `2026-07-28` version and capabilities inside `params._meta`.
It also supports the optional `server/discover` request. Modern requests do not
use `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `Mcp-Session-Id`, the HTTP GET
stream, or a session DELETE. `MCP-Protocol-Version` and `Mcp-Method` are set
for each request. `Mcp-Name` is set for `tools/call`, `prompts/get`, and
`resources/read`, using `params.name` or `params.uri` as appropriate.

Header values requiring escaping are represented as `=?base64?...?=` following
the protocol's sentinel encoding. The transport caches validated
`x-mcp-header` parameter annotations from modern `tools/list` responses
(including nested direct properties) and mirrors applicable tool arguments into
`Mcp-Param-*` headers. Invalid annotated tool schemas are excluded from the
modern list. A direct `tools/call` **before** `tools/list` might lack schema-
derived headers; clients should list tools first when using annotated tools.

Modern requests are routed independently and retain the originating client's
`_meta`. Two clients' identical JSON-RPC IDs are remapped by the broker; modern
clients are not merged into an already-initialized legacy stdio session.
Normal modern JSON/SSE results, including multi-round-trip `input_required`
results, are forwarded as received. MRTR input collection remains the calling
client's responsibility. The current finite request timeout does not promise
an indefinite `subscriptions/listen` stream, and no automatic stream restart
or SSE cursor resumption is claimed.

### Explicit transport boundaries

The legacy initialization/session/JSON/SSE path targets 2025 Streamable HTTP,
including 2025-03-26/2025-06-18 and ordinary 2025-11-25 streams. It does **not**
implement SSE cursor resumption, `Last-Event-ID`
or the 2025-11-25 polling behavior where a server closes a POST stream before its
result and expects GET resumption. Such an incomplete POST stream returns a
correlated error; the operation is not replayed. Unsolicited GET reconnection is
not lossless and does not replay missed events.

OAuth 2.1 authorization is available through the official Go MCP SDK with an
explicitly configured `oauth` block and `agentcfg auth login <server>`.
Discovery, PKCE, encrypted cached tokens and refresh are supported; the broker
never initiates an interactive login or opens a browser without a user command.
The configured redirect URL must be registered with the authorization provider.
Windows uses per-user DPAPI, while Linux/macOS need an explicitly supplied
`AGENTCFG_OAUTH_KEY` (base64-encoded 32 random bytes) or an injected secure
store. Static configured headers are supported without OAuth; a configured
literal Authorization header cannot be combined with OAuth. HTTP 401/403
failures without valid credentials return sanitized errors. Legacy 2024
HTTP+SSE (`type: "sse"`, with
a separate server-selected POST endpoint) is explicitly unsupported. There is no
implicit fallback to that protocol and no endpoint supplied by SSE is followed.

## Vérification manuelle de Huh

Dans un environnement de test avec un home isolé et des fixtures de harnesses,
vérifier d'abord le flux `agentcfg init` :

1. `agentcfg init --plain` découvre les MCP et skills natifs et affiche un plan sans créer de fichier.
2. `agentcfg init` demande les harnesses de destination, puis une seule confirmation avant l'import et la migration.
3. Après validation, les MCP JSON/JSONC et TOML Codex utilisent les proxies agentcfg ; les sources upstream n'existent que sous `~/.agentcfg/`.
4. Les skills natifs sont centralisés puis copiés physiquement dans les destinations choisies ; les anciennes sources, y compris celles des harnesses non sélectionnés, sont retirées avec sauvegarde.
5. `agentcfg init --yes` autorise le parcours complet ; `init --plain` ne modifie aucun fichier.
6. Un import incomplet ou ambigu bloque init. Une erreur pendant la migration tente de restaurer l'état natif et archive les sources importées. `restore` doit rétablir les configurations et skills d'origine.
7. Pour les modifications ultérieures, `agentcfg sync --plain` prévisualise les changements et `agentcfg sync --apply --yes` autorise leur application.

Lancer ensuite `agentcfg config`, puis vérifier que :

1. Configuration et Inventory présentent les quatre catégories avec compteurs numériques alignés, puis `Refresh` et `Exit`, via Huh Select. Le compteur Harnesses correspond aux harnesses activés, pas au nombre d'adaptateurs supportés ; Refresh recharge sans écrire.
2. Les cases cochées apparaissent seulement dans les listes de disponibilités multiples ; annuler une édition ne modifie rien.
3. Les entrées Diagnostics et Synchronize sont absentes du menu principal ; `agentcfg status`, `agentcfg validate` et `agentcfg sync` restent disponibles. La prévisualisation de synchronisation reste en lecture seule avant confirmation et application.
4. Les détails, avertissements et conflits sont lisibles sur le terminal cible.

Rejouer ces parcours avec des inventaires vides, un seul élément et plus de
